stories.title: Flagship Restoration Project in Brazil's Cerrado Savannah Working to Restore 4.4 Million Acres
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: Brazil's Cerrado savanna, a vast tropical grassland that's home to incredible wildlife, is getting a huge helping hand. A restoration program there was just honored at a UN conference as one of the three most ambitious and effective ecosystem-repair efforts happening anywhere in the world right now. The project is already working to bring back native plants and habitat across 4.4 million acres, an area roughly the size of Massachusetts. It's proof that large-scale land healing isn't just a dream, it's actually underway.
stories.why_good: A real, ongoing restoration effort recognized by international experts for its scale and effectiveness in healing a critical ecosystem.

stories.title: Scientists Pioneer Chemical Bath Method to Restore Aging EV Batteries Without Breaking Them Down
stories.label: technology
stories.summary: Cornell University scientists have found a clever way to bring old electric car batteries back to life. Instead of tearing a worn-out battery apart to recycle its materials, they give it a special chemical bath that restores much of its lost range and power. This could save huge amounts of energy and money compared to building brand-new recycling plants. It's a small process with a big potential payoff for making electric cars more affordable and sustainable in the long run.
stories.why_good: A real, demonstrated fix for a major clean-energy bottleneck (battery degradation) that could cut waste and costs without new factories.

stories.title: Bikes Outnumbered Cars on Scottish Rush Hour Route for the First Time Ever
stories.label: earth
stories.summary: In Edinburgh, more people rode bikes than drove cars during a May morning rush hour, a first in the city's history. It happened thanks to new protected bike lanes and popular e-bike rental schemes making cycling safer and easier. Cycling Scotland tracked the numbers and confirmed the milestone across several busy routes. It's a real sign that when cities build safe places to cycle, people happily leave their cars at home. Less traffic and cleaner air for everyone who lives there.
stories.why_good: A measurable, real shift toward greener commuting driven by actual infrastructure investment, not a plan or forecast.
